newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sees 97 copper output rising to 3.4 mln tns.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees 97 copper output rising to 3.4 mln tns.

text.p: Chile expects copper production to rise to 3.4 million tonnes this year, up from 3.1 million tonnes in 1996 as new mines come on line and expansions are completed, said government board Cochilco.
Copper output is likely to climb to 4.86 million tonnes by the end of the decade, said the Comision Chilena del Cobre (Cochilco) in a report on foreign investment in the mining industry.
Cochilco expects gold production to climb to 78 tonnes by 2000 from 52 tonnes last year.
Foreign investment in the all-important mining sector slumped last year to $886 million from $1.7 billion in 1995 and a similar level in 1994, said the report.
"If we look at the long term, this (1996) figure is not really low as investment in 1994 and 1995 were extremely high," Cochilco expert Marco Fluckiger told the news conference.
Cochilco expects foreign investment in the industry to climb this year to $1.3 billion with privately owned foreign mines producing an increasing share of Chile's overall copper output.
"The important growth of foreign investment has had a resulting impact on production which will become more significant in coming years," said the report.
Production from the recently completed El Abra mine will be the largest factor behind the nine percent rise in Chilean copper production this year, it said.
El Abra, which is owned by Cyprus Minerals and state copper firm Codelco, will produce at least 225,000 tonnes of copper cathodes this year.
Output from foreign companies will soar to three million tonnes by 2000 from 1.6 million tonnes last year.
State copper production will rise just 400,000 tonnes over the same period to 1.8 million tonnes.
